chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah from Muawiya ibn Hukaym from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira said:

I asked Abdullah ibn Bukayr about a man who divorced his wife once, then left her until she became irrevocably divorced from him, then he married her. He said: 'She is with him as she was in the marriage.'
I said to him, 'For the report of Rifah states: if there is a husband between them.' So Abdullah said to me, 'This is a husband, and this is from what Allah has granted of opinion.'

And when he divorces her once, so she becomes irrevocably divorced from him, then she marries another husband. Then her husband divorces her, so she marries her former husband, so she is with him accepted as she used to be.
I said to Abdullah, 'With whose report is this?' So he said, 'This is from what Allah has granted.'
Muawiya ibn Hukaym said: 'Our companions narrated from Rifah ibn Musa that the husband demolishes the first divorce. So if he marries her, she is with him accepted.'
So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The third demolishes, and the first and the second do not.'
And the report of Rifah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) is that which Ibn Bukayh argues by.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between a single divorce and a triple divorce regarding the need for an intermediate marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the Shia jurisprudential distinction between *talaq raj'i* (revocable divorce) and *talaq ba'in* (irrevocable divorce), specifically addressing the condition of *naskh al-'aqd* (cancellation of the contract) through a subsequent marriage. While the majority view cited from Rifah ibn Musa holds that a single or double divorce is not fully demolished by remarriage to a third party, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that only a triple divorce or a specific irrevocable ruling necessitates a new marriage contract to restore the original marital status. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the husband's right to reconcile without a *muhrir* (intermediary marriage) for the first two divorces, contrasting with other schools of thought.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muawiya Bin Hukeym, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira who said,

‘I asked Abdullah Bin Bukeyr about a man who divorces his wife once, then leaves her until she irrevocably divorced from him. Then he re-marries her. He said, ‘She is with him as she was regarding the marriage’.

I said to him, So in the report of Rafa’at is, ‘When there is a husband between the two’. So Abdullah said to me, ‘This is a husband, and this is from what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Granted from the opinion,

and when he divorces her once, so she becomes irrevocably divorced from him, then she marries another husband. Then her husband divorces her, so she marries her former husband, so she would be with him accepted as she used to be’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘So I said to Abdullah, ‘With whose report is this, ‘So he said, ‘This is from what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Granted’?’
He said, ‘Muawiya Bin Hukeym reported, from our companions, from Rafa’at Bin Musa that the husband demolishes the first divorce. So if he were to marry her, so she would be with him, acceptable’.
So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The third (divorce) demolishes, and the first and the second do not’.
And in a report of Rafa’at, from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, it is that which Ibn Bukeyr argues by’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah has narrated from Mu‘awiyah ibn Hakam from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who divorces his wife and leaves until she becomes stranger to him, then marries her. He (the Imam) said, ‘She can live with him just as she did with marriage.’
I then said, ‘Hadith of Rifa‘ah says, “If there is a husband in between.’” Then ‘Abd Allah said to me, ‘This is husband and it is what Allah has granted of opinion.
Whenever he divorces once and then she becomes stranger to him, then another man marries her then her husband divorces, then she marries the first husband, she can live with him accepted as she was.’
I then asked ‘Abd Allah, ‘According to whose Hadith is this?’ He replied, ‘It is what Allah has granted.’
Mu‘awiyah ibn Hukaym has said that our people have narrated from Rifa‘ah ibn Musa that husband destroys the first divorce and if he marries her she lives with him accepted.’
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘Three divorces destroy but not one and two.’
Hadith of Rifa‘ah from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, is the one on the basis of which ibn Bukayr has argued.’”
